home.title: One JSON file. One HTML file. That's the site.

cards.title: hi, welcome to the demo
cards.body:
Everything you're looking at right now came out of a single site_data.json file and got compiled into one self-contained index.html by a ~450-line Python script with zero dependencies. No node_modules. No bundler. No framework. There is no build step you need to fear.

Click around. The nav on the right, the routes, the little tools, the gallery, the synth — all of it is data.

cards.title: the pitch
cards.body:
SPDRM started in 2022 as a WordPress replacement: a newspaper layout with a sticky header and footer, independently scrolling regions, and every piece of content living in a variable instead of a page file. The page responds to navigation dynamically — that's the whole "Dynamic Response Model" thing.

It has been quietly serving real sites since. This repo is it, cleaned up and set free.

cards.title: what to poke at
cards.body: The Tools section has interactive routes (palindrome checker, pig latin, a frame-rate converter) — those are just HTML strings in the JSON with an optional onload hook. The Gallery is a route type. The Synth is an optional module. The Abyss is a route type, not a joke. Well. Both.

cards.title: why it exists
cards.body:
Because updating a WordPress site meant logging into a dashboard, and updating this site means editing a JSON file and running one command. One of those feels like work. The other feels like publishing.

The builder validates your whole site before it writes anything — bad route, bad nav slug, missing field, the build dies loudly instead of shipping quietly broken.

cards.title: honest limitations
cards.body: Routing is hash-based (#about) and uses location.replace, so the back button leaves the site instead of walking your route history — that's deliberate for now, and a History API router is on the roadmap for v0.2. SEO meta is set client-side after render. The minifier is a conservative regex pass, not a real one. All of this is in the SPEC, in writing, where it can't be denied.

overview.title: Overview
meta: What SPDRM is, in two cards.

cards.title: What is SPDRM?
cards.body: SPDRM (Single Page Dynamic Response Model) is a lightweight framework for creating single-page sites using vanilla JavaScript. No build tools, no dependencies — just HTML, CSS, and JS. A stdlib-Python builder turns your content into one self-contained page.

cards.title: Quick Facts
cards.body:
Language: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+)
Builder: Python 3, stdlib only
Dependencies: Zero
Server requirements: None (static files only)
Routing: Hash-based declarative route objects
Rendering: Dynamic DOM manipulation via utility functions

getting-started.title: Getting Started
meta: How to set up and run an SPDRM application.

cards.title: Setup
cards.body: Clone the repo and build: python3 spdrm/build.py, then serve the root with any static file server (python3 -m http.server 8000). No package install, no bundler, no server requirements. The builder validates the entire site and writes index.html, manifest.json, and sitemap.xml.

cards.title: File Structure
cards.body:
The moving parts:

spdrm/build.py — the builder (validate, minify, assemble)
spdrm/site_data.json — your whole site: routes, nav, meta, layout
spdrm/src/ — the runtime: router.js, utils.js, tools.js, style.css (+ optional modules)
index.html — generated, never hand-edit

Editing content means editing the JSON (or using the Tkinter editor, spdrm/gui_editor.py) and rebuilding.

cards.title: Deploying
cards.body: The output is static files, so any host works: Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Apache, nginx, a Raspberry Pi on a shelf. Hash routing means no server rewrites anywhere. Full recipes are in docs/deploying.md.

architecture.title: Architecture
meta: The declarative routing model behind SPDRM.

cards.title: Concept
cards.body: SPDRM is a declarative routing model. Instead of routing logic scattered across switch statements or external libraries, each page or view is defined as an entry in a routes object with properties that tell the router how to render it.

cards.title: Route types
cards.body:
In site_data.json, every route has a type:

content — title + cards (the card is the one UI primitive everything is made of)
interactive — raw HTML plus an optional onload hook (the tools use this)
gallery — rows of {src, title} images, click one to zoom it in the modal
iframe — embeds a URL
abyss — full-screen canvas RGB noise. It is what it sounds like.
404 — error body, auto-redirects home

cards.title: Route Properties
cards.body:
At runtime the router (move()) inspects the route's properties to determine how to render it:

title — Sets a page heading via initmain(title)
render() — Function that populates content (usually calling createCard())
iframe — URL for an embedded iframe; if present, title/render are skipped
bgImage — URL for a full-page background image with CSS blend-mode
is404 — Flag for 404/redirect routes
isAbyss — Flag for canvas noise generator routes
meta — Array of [title, description, keywords] for SEO

cards.title: Dispatcher Logic
cards.body:
The router checks route properties in priority order:

1. If is404 — render error, update URL, load meta, return
2. If isAbyss — clear content, run randimg(), update URL, load meta, return
3. If iframe — embed the iframe, update URL, load meta, return
4. If title — initialize the page heading
5. If bgImage — set background image on main
6. If render — call the render function
7. Always — generate a random ad (renders nothing if the ads array is empty), update URL hash, load SEO meta

cards.title: Content Lifecycle
cards.body:
When a route is activated, the content area is cleared and rebuilt in this sequence:

initmain(title) → bgImage → route.render() → generateAd() → moveurl(s) → loadmeta()

api-index.title: API: index.js
meta: Core SPDRM functions: routes, move, loadnav, moveurl, loadmeta.

cards.title: siteData
cards.body: Global configuration object with title, seotitle (appended to document titles), and tagline.

cards.title: routes
cards.body: The central routing table. Each key is a URL slug, and each value is a route config object. The router looks up routes[s] and falls back to routes.home if the key doesn't exist. Properties: title, render(), iframe, bgImage, is404, isAbyss, meta.

cards.title: move(s)
cards.body: Main router. Accepts a route key string, looks it up in routes, dispatches by property inspection (iframe, is404, isAbyss, title, bgImage, render), updates URL hash, and loads SEO meta.

cards.title: loadnav()
cards.body: Builds the sidebar navigation from an array of nav item objects. Each item can have title, click, and nested children (sub-nav items). Rendered as an unordered list.

cards.title: moveurl(s)
cards.body: Updates window.location.hash to reflect the current page. Uses window.location.replace so the hash changes without creating extra history entries.

cards.title: loadmeta(title, desc, keywords)
cards.body: Updates the page <title> and meta[name=description] and meta[name=keywords] attributes for SEO.

cards.title: window.onload
cards.body: Entry point. Reads window.location.hash, strips the #, and calls move(hash). Falls back to routes.home if the hash is empty or doesn't match any route.

api-utils.title: API: utils.js
meta: DOM helpers: html, createCard, zoomimg, randimg, mandelbrot, and more.

cards.title: html(strings, ...values)
cards.body: Tagged template literal for safe DOM construction. Escapes HTML in string values but allows Node objects to be interpolated directly. Returns a single element or document fragment.

cards.title: initmain(title)
cards.body: Clears main and appends a styled heading element with mainhead class and the given title.

cards.title: createCard(title, post, more)
cards.body: Creates a styled card component with an optional header, body text (innerHTML), and an optional appended element. Cards are appended to main.

cards.title: generateAd()
cards.body: Picks a random ad from the ads array in site_data and appends it to main. Renders nothing when the array is empty. Routes can opt out with ads: false.

cards.title: appendP(parent, text)
cards.body: Appends a small superscript-styled paragraph to a given parent element.

cards.title: zoomimg(s)
cards.body: Opens an image in a modal <dialog> element (the shakey one). Expects an object with .src and .title — a [src, title] array works too. The gallery route type wires this up for you.

cards.title: generateDialog(title, message)
cards.body: Opens a general-purpose modal dialog with a message and close button.

cards.title: randimg()
cards.body: Generates a full-size canvas filled with random RGB noise and appends it to main. Used by isAbyss routes.

cards.title: devclick()
cards.body: Dev toolbar toggle. Appends utility buttons to the sidebar for debugging: open modal, test API.

cards.title: isValidEmail(email)
cards.body: Returns true/false based on RFC-compatible email regex validation.

cards.title: maybeAnimate()
cards.body: Randomly triggers a blur animation on elements with class .blurry-vision (50% chance). Pair it with the shakey dialog class for the full house style.

cards.title: createMandelbrotSVG(width, height, element, arr)
cards.body: Generates an interactive SVG Mandelbrot set renderer, drawing pixel-by-pixel into the given element. Iterations and scale are controlled via the arr parameter.

cards.title: calculateMandelbrotValue(x, y, w, h, arr)
cards.body: Core Mandelbrot iteration function. Returns the iteration count at which the point escapes the set, used by createMandelbrotSVG for coloring.
